steps: Fill in the two-household budget so you know what you can afford monthly.
Ask each lawyer for estimated hours per phase and enter them for each scenario.
Add your state's filing fee and expected outside costs (mediator, appraisals).
Compare the totals; they show what a dispute costs compared with an agreement.
After hiring, log deposits and invoices in the retainer tracker.
forWho: People considering or starting a divorce who want a realistic budget
Anyone deciding between mediation and litigation on cost grounds
People already paying a retainer who want to track it
notFor: Anyone needing advice on custody, support or property division: speak to a family lawyer
People in danger: contact the National Domestic Violence Hotline (1-800-799-7233) or 911

compat: Excel 365, LibreOffice Calc 7+ and Google Sheets (File → Import; sheet protection is not carried over). PDFs are US Letter and fillable in Adobe Acrobat Reader and most browser PDF viewers.
limits: It does not calculate child support or alimony (each state has its own formula).
It does not decide what is marital or separate property.
It is not legal or financial advice.

faq.q: Does it include my state's filing fee?
faq.a: The workbook lists the divorce filing fee we verified for each state, with the official source, as of October 2026. Where a fee varies by county or was not verified, it says so. Always confirm with your court clerk.

faq.q: Can a divorce lawyer work on contingency?
faq.a: No. ABA Model Rule 1.5(d), adopted in some form by most states, bars contingency fees that depend on securing a divorce or the amount of support or property. That is why budgeting the hourly fees matters.
